title: I Posted the Metal-Detector Beach-Zone Hours After They Swept My Square

parts.text: I staked square C at 6:03 a.m. and permittee Holst was already sweeping our numbered grid. The kiosk said: ONE SQUARE. TWO HOURS. GRID STAYS WITH THE PERMIT. I was forty-eight, club member, holding a permit that listed our zone. Holst shrugged. "Permits are the beach." I photographed the kiosk, the permit, and his coil on our pin. Then I asked for the zone log. At 6:11 parks pinged why Holst's name was on our square. I kept my voice dune-quiet and let the timestamp talk. A kiosk is only a kiosk until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: Parks can see Holst's coil on our pin during our square.

social.video_title: He swept our numbered grid on our beach zone — Part 1/2
social.description: Beach zone, a permittee on our pin, a two-hour kiosk he posted. I logged the coil. Would you have asked for the zone log?

parts.text: Holst called it a fringe until parks asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the kiosk, and the coil still. The square went back to our stakes. Holst ran his own two hours and told the next permittee atmosphere was always about targets. Targets is a word permittees use when a grid exists. Zone policy now has a second line: PERMITS ARE NOT THE BEACH. I keep our stakes on a labeled bag. Holst brown-bags his jokes. The dune finally looks like a permit, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Permits are not the beach — Part 2/2
social.description: Zone log, numbered grid, and a second line on the kiosk. Was a fringe ever our pin?
